Triggering Builds

payload.markdown: All of this rich information is almost useless if someone in your team must remember to kick off each build with a manual click. Naturally, Jenkins provides mechanisms by which builds can be automatically triggered.

blocks.text: All of this rich information is almost useless if someone in your team must remember to kick off each build with a manual click. Naturally, Jenkins provides mechanisms by which builds can be automatically triggered.

payload.markdown: You can set Jenkins to build at fixed intervals or to poll the version control repository, again at specified intervals. Intervals can be set using cron format, which provides fine, although somewhat arcane, control over scheduling. Luckily, Jenkins provides good online help for the format, and there are simple aliases if you don’t require precision scheduling. The aliases include @hourly, @midnight, @daily, @weekly, and @monthly. In Figure 21-13, I configure the build to run once daily, or every time the repository changes, based upon a poll for changes that should take place once an hour.

🧠 Key concepts

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
HTTP & REST: Designing HTTP endpoints as resources with predictable methods and status codes.
Namespaces: Named scopes that prevent class-name collisions and organise code.
Properties & Methods: Class state held in properties, and behaviour implemented as methods.
Static & Constants: Members belonging to the class itself rather than to any one instance.
Static Analysis: Finding type and logic bugs without running the code, with PHPStan or Psalm.
Variables: Named storage for a value; PHP infers the type from what you assign.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.

8678.title: Here is a part of a class named Validate in the namespace userthing\util
8678.code:
<?php
public function validateUser(string $mail, string $pass): bool
{
    // make it always fail
    // return false;
    $user = $this->store->getUser($mail);
    if (is_null($user)) {
        return false;
    }
    $testpass = $user->getPass();
    if ($testpass == $pass) {
        return true;
    }
    $this->store->notifyPasswordFailure($mail);
    return false;
}
